O.content: The title visibly reads "Units Sold by Product (Weekend Pop-up)" and the vertical-axis label visibly reads "Units Sold".
Visible tick inscriptions include "2,000", "4,000", "6,000", "8,000", and "10,000" at vertically aligned tick marks.
A dark-red bar is visibly positioned above the x-axis label "Product A"; its top is below the visible "2,000" tick and above the baseline.

B.text: If the chart’s vertical axis encodes Units Sold on a linear scale and each labeled bar is bound to its product label, Product A’s bar can be interpolated at about 1,700 units. Under the supplied policy, a value less than 500 units from a decision threshold falls in the manual merchandising verification variance band. Selecting the manual-check route requires the additional assumption that this overlapping variance-band rule applies as the operative route rather than being subordinate to the base sales tier.
B.conditions: Applies only if the y-axis is linear, the Product A bar is correctly attached to its label, the visual interpolation is sufficiently accurate, and the manual variance band takes precedence or independently determines the route.
